texts: Write a doha about how a harsh word, once dropped like a pebble into a deep well, can never be drawn up again, and how a potter handles clay gently, as a wise person handles speech.
doha: words are like clay, speak gently, and bad words fall in a well
Gentle as the potter's palm on wet clay be the word, for once it falls in the well, none may draw it back.
I said something cruel to my best friend, a potter, in anger last week, and now it's like I dropped it down a well; I can't take it back, and he hasn't called.
words, well, potter
sweet words, sandalwood
My grandmother never raises her voice, and her gentle manner calms the whole house, the way sandalwood cools the skin.
Sweet words are sandalwood on the heated heart, and cool both speaker and listener.
Write a doha about gentle speech that cools the listener's heart like sandalwood paste on a burning forehead, and how a kind word spoken at the right moment can heal where medicine fails.
doha: speak sweetly like sandalwood
In the market of voices, the sweet word is the tree whose shade is sought by all.
words, tree, market
Compose a doha about a person who speaks sweetly in the noisy market, whose words are like the shade of a tree to weary shoppers, drawing friends and customers without needing to shout.
doha: sweet talk in the market, like shade of a tree
Our vegetable seller at the market sits under a big tree and is always gentle with everyone and has a huge line at his stall, while the loud sellers next to him stand empty.
Please write a doha about the power of words, how a single kind sentence can lift a person's spirits for days, and how one cruel remark can hurt for years, so we must choose what we say with care.
doha on speaking kindly pls
mind your words
A word once spoken cannot be called back; speak, then, as if it will live forever.
My father said something harsh to me at dinner ten years ago and I still remember exactly how it felt.
Write a doha about a potter who handles clay gently under a tree and speaks softly to his apprentices, a picture of how kindness in speech shapes people the way careful hands shape a vessel.
Soft as the potter's hands on clay, the word that shapes a heart; the tree bears witness.
My art teacher used to work with clay under the big tree in our school yard, and the way he talked to us, never harshly, is why I still make things today.
gentle words, potter, tree
doha: speaking softly like a potter w clay under a tree
At the market last night a vendor lit a lamp and spoke so gently to a crying child that the whole stall seemed calmer.

Compose a doha about a lamp burning in the corner of a busy market and a vendor whose sweet words warm everyone who stops, showing how kindness in speech can bring comfort in the midst of noise and haggling.
doha: lamp in the market, kind words from the seller
market, lamp, kind words
In the market's roar, one gentle voice is a lamp that draws the weary near.
The sweet word is a tree beside the road, giving shade to every passing heart.
Write a doha comparing a kind and thoughtful word to a tree that gives shade to every traveller, free of cost, while a bitter word is like an axe that cuts without reason and leaves only a stump.
kind words, tree
My neighbour always has something encouraging to say, and every time I talk to him I feel like I've been resting under a big calm tree.
doha: sweet words are like a tree's shade
potter, gentle words

Compose a doha about the way words shape people as a potter shapes clay, and how a gentle word moulds a person while a rough one cracks him, so the wise measure each sentence before it leaves their lips.
doha: words shape people like a potter shapes clay
As clay yields to the potter's palm, so hearts yield to the soft word and crack at the hard one.
My grandfather the potter never once shouted at me, and the gentle way he spoke is why I'm the person I am today.
At the boat landing near the market, the ferryman greeted everyone with a smile and a kind word, and people went out of their way to cross with him.
doha: boat and market, sweet words
A kind word is a boat in the market's rough waters, carrying the weary home.

Write a doha about a boatman near the busy market whose gentle words and friendly voice make him the most sought-after on the shore, showing that sweet speech draws people more than any promise of speed.
market, boat, sweet words
I got into a fight with my sister last month and said something I didn't mean, and ever since, our calls have been awkward.
A sweet word costs nothing and wins the world; a harsh one costs the world and wins nothing.
Write a doha about how a person who speaks sweetly makes friends of strangers and a person who speaks bitterly makes enemies of friends, and how the choice is made fresh every time we open our mouth.
kind speech
doha pls about talking nicely to people
prayer beads, sweet words
Better one kind word than ten thousand beads counted with a bitter tongue.
doha: kind words > counting prayer beads
My aunt chants with her prayer beads all morning and then criticises everyone in the family by lunchtime.

Compose a doha about how counting prayer beads all day is worth nothing if the tongue that recites them also speaks harshly of others, and how one sweet word to a neighbour is worth more than a thousand chants.
kind words, tree
Speak as the tree gives: freely, softly, and to all who stop beneath.
The old teacher in our village never says an unkind word, and every child who passes his tree-shaded door stops to talk with him.
Write a doha about how a kind and sweet word is like the shade of a tree, welcoming and cooling to anyone who comes near, and how a harsh word is like a barren place that drives all travellers away.
doha: kind speech like shade of a tree
Light the lamp of a sweet word and the dark mind clears; the beads may rest.
During evening prayers I noticed my uncle, who has his prayer beads and lamp ready every night, snapped at his wife about dinner, and the calm of the whole evening was gone.
doha: the lamp and prayer beads mean nothing if your words are harsh

Compose a doha about the devotee who lights a lamp and counts prayer beads at dusk, yet speaks harshly to his household, teaching that gentle speech is the true devotion and all the rest is only decoration.
lamp, beads, kind words
doha: sweet talk like sandalwood on a boat ride
A word of sandalwood on a boat of silence, and the whole river is perfumed.
On our boat ride to the island, a kind old lady spoke so gently to the nervous kids that everyone around her relaxed, like there was sandalwood in the air.
boat, sandalwood, kind words
Write a doha about a boatman whose sweet speech is like sandalwood, calming every passenger on the crossing, because a gentle voice is a gift that costs nothing and perfumes the entire journey.

Compose a doha about a fish caught by a sweet-looking lure and a person caught by flattering words, showing that speech can be a hook, and that we should choose our words and those we trust with care.
The fish takes the bait of the sweet word and the hook is hidden in the voice.
fish, honeyed words
doha: fish and sweet talk, don't believe flatterers
A salesman charmed my father with such sweet words that he bought a plan he didn't need, and he realised only later that he'd been hooked like a fish.
My teacher used to say that the tongue has no bones but it can break bones, and I have only recently understood what he meant.
Please write a doha about the force of a spoken word, how it can build or destroy a relationship in an instant, and how we should treat our speech as something sacred and powerful, not casual.
The tongue has no bones, yet it breaks hearts; guard it as you would guard a treasure.
doha on watching what you say
careful words
doha: potter + prayer beads + sweet words
potter, beads, kind words
Write a doha about a potter who counts his prayer beads but never speaks a harsh word to his apprentices, showing that his gentle speech shapes better vessels and better people than any ritual.
The potter's prayer is not in his beads but in the softness of his word.
My uncle, a potter, was never seen without his prayer beads, but what everyone remembered about him at his memorial was that he never said a cruel thing to anyone.
My manager never raises his voice, even when things go wrong, and somehow everyone works harder for him than for the shouting types.
doha: calm words are stronger than shouting

Write a doha about a person who speaks with calm and kindness even in the middle of conflict, and how such speech wins hearts that shouting could never win, because gentleness has its own quiet strength.
Soft is the voice that conquers, and loud the one that loses.
gentle strength of words
I told a colleague his idea was stupid in front of everyone yesterday, and the look on his face is going to stay with me for a while.
need a doha about thinking before speaking
think before speaking

Compose a doha about the habit of pausing before speaking, so that sharp or careless words never escape, because once words leave the mouth they cannot be taken back, and kindness can then guide our speech.
Let the heart weigh the word before the tongue lets it go.

Write a doha about a boatman whose gentle words are like sandalwood paste, easing the fear of every passenger crossing the water, and showing that sweet speech is both a boat and a balm for troubled people.
boat, sandalwood, sweet words
doha: kind words as sandalwood & a boat for the soul
When I was terrified of the river crossing, the boatman spoke so softly and kindly that my fear faded away like the scent of sandalwood fading into air.
Sweet words are a boat, and sandalwood their fragrance, bearing the worried safely over.
doha: a moth drawn to sweet words
moth, sweet words
The moth is drawn to a gentle word, as hearts are drawn to kindness.
My cousin is always surrounded by people who flutter around him like moths because he never has an unkind word for anyone.
Compose a doha about a person whose sweet speech draws friends the way sweetness draws a moth, so that people gather around him without being asked, simply for the pleasure of his gentle company.
Write a doha about the way a kind word is a lamp in a dark moment, steadying a frightened person and showing him the way forward, though the speaker may never know the difference it made.
lamp, kind words
When I was going through a rough time, a stranger told me you will be fine in such a steady voice that it was like someone had lit a lamp in a dark room.
A kind word is a lamp in the night; the speaker never knows who walks by it.
doha: kind words as a lamp
Compose a doha about the potter who shapes clay vessels with soft, patient hands, a picture of the way a wise person shapes the character of the people he talks to with kind and gentle speech.
doha: speak softly like a potter shaping clay
My pottery teacher criticised my work in the softest voice, so it never felt like criticism, and I improved faster than I ever did with the shouting teachers.
potter, soft words
The potter's palm is gentle and the word is gentler, for clay and heart alike remember what shapes them.
Sweetness in what we say is the sweetest gift, and free for all who give.
My new neighbour greeted me with a warm smile and a few kind words on my first day, and I've felt at home here ever since.
Write a doha on how a warm greeting and a few gentle words can turn a stranger into a friend and a difficult day into a happy one, because kindness in speech is the cheapest and most valuable gift.
doha: be nice to people with your words
sweet words
doha: sweet words like sandalwood
A sweet word is sandalwood on the tongue, cooling the speaker and the one who hears.
My grandmother's voice is so gentle that people tell their secrets to her within minutes, and I've often thought it is like sandalwood: you feel it before you know it.
Compose a doha about gentle speech that, like sandalwood, spreads coolness and fragrance among those who hear it, and how the speaker is himself refreshed by the kindness he gives.
sandalwood, sweet words
Write a doha about the way sandalwood keeps its fragrance when it is cut or rubbed, and how a wise person keeps his sweet speech even when insulted, answering harsh words with gentle ones.
doha: speak sweetly even when insulted, like sandalwood
Cut the sandalwood and it perfumes the blade; answer harshness with sweetness, and so be remembered.
sandalwood, sweet words
A customer yelled at me for something that wasn't my fault yesterday, and I answered as kindly as I could, like sandalwood under the grinding stone, and by the end she apologized.
lamp, well, kind words
At the village well last evening, a woman spoke so kindly to a stranger that a small crowd gathered around her, as if she carried a lamp.
Write a doha about a person at the well who speaks sweetly to everyone who comes for water, her words a lamp to the lonely, so that her company is sought as much as the water she draws.
Her words are a lamp at the well, and the thirsty come for more than water.
doha: kind words at the well, like a lamp
I snapped at my mom over nothing today, and now I can't stop thinking about how tired she looked.
words that hurt
A moment's temper, a lifetime's regret; the tongue's slip leaves the longest scar.
need a doha about regretting angry words
Write a doha about the regret that follows sharp words spoken in anger, how they cannot be taken back, and how a person must learn to hold his tongue before it wounds the people he loves most.
doha: words you speak are like a well, they come back to you
Compose a doha about a well that echoes whatever is said into it, kind words returning as kind and harsh ones as harsh, a picture of how the speech we give to others returns to us in the same form.
The well returns the voice you give; so sing, or shout, and be answered.
well, echo, words
I shouted into the old well in our village as a child and heard my voice come back, and I think of it now when I see how people treat me as I treat them.

Write a doha about speech as the mirror of the heart, showing a person's real character, so that a gentle speaker reveals a gentle soul and a bitter speaker a troubled one, each known by the words they choose.
Tell me how a man speaks, and I will know what lives in his heart.
your words reveal you
doha: your words show who you are
I met a woman at the bus stop who spoke to everyone so warmly that I knew exactly what kind of person she was before she told me anything.
My teenager has started answering back in a really rude way, and I'm trying to figure out how to teach him that tone matters as much as words.
doha about speaking respectfully to elders
respectful words
A courteous word welcomes everyone, and a rude one turns the world away.
Write a doha about the importance of speaking respectfully, even to those who disagree with us, and about how courtesy in speech is the mark of a mature mind and the surest path to being heard.
After a long argument with my husband I realized the fight was never about chores, it was about the tone we used on each other.
tone of voice
Not the word but the tone, not the tone but the heart behind it, decides what is heard.
doha: speak softly in arguments
Compose a doha about how the manner in which we speak, soft or sharp, matters as much as what we say, and how gentle speech can end an argument while harshness only makes it grow.
Write a doha about a boat that carries people over troubled waters as sweet words carry people through troubled times, and how both ask only that someone takes care to steer them with gentleness.
doha: kind words are like a boat for sad people
When my friend was grieving, I didn't know what to say, so I just spoke softly for an hour, and she later said it was like I had rowed her to shore in a boat.
A kind word is a boat in a sea of sorrow, carrying the weary toward calm.
boat, kind speech
In my village there's a big tree where people sit and talk, and whoever speaks gently there is always the one everyone listens to.
Beneath the tree, the sweet word is heard; the loud one is lost in the leaves.
Write a doha about a gathering under a tree where the person who speaks softly and sweetly is heard by all, while the loud and the harsh are ignored, showing that gentleness has a quiet authority.
tree, gentle speech
doha: people under a tree, the kind speaker wins
doha on kind words please
A tiny compliment from a stranger on the train this morning made my entire week, and I want to remember how powerful that was.
kind words

Compose a doha about the way a simple kind word, offered to a stranger without expecting anything in return, can brighten a day, heal a wound, and travel on from one heart to another in a chain of goodness.
A word of kindness, lightly given, lives longer than any grand gift.
Write a doha about a moth that is drawn to the sandalwood fragrance of a gentle voice, showing that sweet speech attracts hearts the way fragrance attracts a moth, without force or demand.
Everyone who meets my aunt seems drawn to her, like moths, because she speaks so gently and warmly, and I think sandalwood is the best way to describe how it feels to be near her.
Sweet voices are sandalwood, and hearts are moths that come without being called.
doha: moth drawn to sandalwood, like people drawn to kind speakers
moth, sandalwood, sweet words
doha: moth + sandalwood + kind words
moth, sandalwood, gentle words
Write a doha about gentle speech that wafts like sandalwood and draws the quiet moths of the heart toward it, so that people come to the soft-spoken person without needing to be invited.
Even the shy kids at school flutter toward my cousin like moths because his voice is so gentle, and he always smells of sandalwood from his morning rituals.
The moth knows the sandalwood by its scent; the heart knows the kind by its voice.
From the tongue of the kind flows sweetness, and the wounded come to be healed.
My grandmother can talk to the angriest person in the village and have them smiling in five minutes, and I've always wondered how she does it.
doha about the power of gentle words
Write a doha about how a person who speaks sweetly and truthfully can calm the angry, comfort the sad and reconcile the quarrelling, using nothing but the gentle force of carefully chosen words.
sweet tongue
gentle words
doha about sweet speech
Whenever I'm upset, my best friend's voice on the phone is the first thing that makes me calm, even before he says anything useful.
Compose a doha about the soothing effect of a soft, loving voice on a troubled mind, and how speaking gently is a gift we can offer anyone at any moment without spending anything.
A gentle voice is balm to the aching heart and costs the giver nothing.
My uncle who fishes talks so softly to everyone, even the moths that gather around him in the evening, that people say even the fish come to him.
Fish to the sweet voice, moth to the kind, and all hearts to the gentle word.
fish, moth, sweet words
doha: fish and moth both come to sweet words
Compose a doha about the way creatures like the fish and the moth are drawn to gentle sounds and calm company, showing that sweet speech reaches even those who cannot understand the words themselves.
I recently apologised to someone I'd wronged years ago, and just saying the words made both of us cry.
Three small words, I was wrong, can heal what years of silence have hurt.
doha: saying sorry kindly
healing words
Write a doha about how a sincere apology spoken gently can mend a friendship that years of silence had damaged, and how our words can be either the source of wounds or the source of healing.
The flower seller at our market greets every single person with a warm word, and her stall is always the first to be visited, though her prices are the same as everyone else's.
In the market of a thousand voices, the sweetest wins the most customers.
doha: sweet words win in the market
market, kind words
Write a doha about a merchant in the busy market whose gentle manner of speaking brings customers and friends alike, showing that sweetness of speech is a better asset than the lowest price.
The moth flies to the soft voice on the boat, as hearts fly to kindness.
Compose a doha about a boatman whose gentle voice draws travellers to his boat the way a moth is drawn to what it loves, showing that sweetness in speech is a magnet no one can resist.
A boatman I know speaks so kindly that people wait for his boat even when others are free, flocking to him like moths.
moth, boat, sweet voice
doha: boat man w sweet voice, people like moths
Under the tree the moth rests, soothed by a voice that never wounds.
At dusk my grandmother sits under the tree and talks gently to the moths that settle near her, and her whole yard seems to calm down.
tree, moth, gentle voice
doha: gentle voice under a tree, even moths come
Write a doha about a gentle speaker sitting under a tree at dusk whose soothing words draw even the moths to rest near him, showing that kindness in speech brings calm to all creatures.
prayer beads, kind words
Compose a doha about a devotee who counts prayer beads but also guards his tongue from harshness, understanding that the gentlest speech is worth more than any amount of ritual repetition.
My aunt turns her prayer beads all morning and then gossips cruelly by afternoon, and I'm trying to tell her, gently, how much more her kindness would mean.
Let the beads be still and the tongue be soft; that is the prayer.
doha: beads don't matter if you talk bad about people
sweet speech
A kind word is a gift that grows in the giving.
Write a doha about the power of speaking sweetly to everyone, regardless of their rank or behavior, and how the habit gradually refines the speaker's own heart until gentleness becomes his nature.
doha: be nice with your words
My father worked as a night guard for thirty years, and he spoke politely to everyone who passed, and half the town came to his retirement because of that.
doha: prayer beads and gentle speech
Beads in the hand, sweetness on the tongue, peace in the heart: this is the whole of prayer.
My grandfather counted his prayer beads daily, and no one in the village ever heard him say a harsh word, and I think the two were connected.
Compose a doha about a devotee who turns his prayer beads and speaks sweetly to all, whose gentle words prove that his prayer has truly changed his heart, rather than merely occupying his hands.
beads, gentle words
Write a doha about a fish lured into a net by the sweet song of a fisherman, a warning that honeyed words can hide harm, and that we should listen to the heart behind the voice.
The fisherman sings sweetly to the fish, and the net is hidden in the song.
doha: sweet talk can trap you like a fish
A fellow at the lake charmed me with such sweet words about an easy investment, and I only realized after paying that I'd been caught like a fish.
fish, honeyed words
Please write a doha about how a harsh word, once let go, cannot be recalled, how it wounds the listener and the conscience of the speaker, and how we should learn to speak only what heals.
I said something unforgivable to my father when I was nineteen, and he's gone now, and I still hear it.
doha: careful with what you say to people you love
The sharp word flies and cannot be called home; the soft one stays and builds a home.
harsh words wound
At my sister's wedding, my uncle gave a speech so warm and humble that even the people who had been fighting for years hugged each other.
kind words heal
One gentle talk, and old quarrels melt into forgiveness.
doha: kind words end fights
Compose a doha about the way a few sincere and gentle words, spoken at the right moment, can heal old wounds and bring estranged people back together, showing the quiet power of kindness.
